author: reek
body: Tightness is checked separately where the transfer function is exact: for add, sub, and neg - no endpoint can overflow in this tiny universe - both endpoints of every kernel answer must be witnessed by a concrete evaluation at the extremal corner pair.

author: reek
body: Operator codes: 1 add, 2 sub, 3 mul, 4 div, 5 mod, 6 min, 7 max are the member-scanned binary operators; 8 union and 9 intersect check membership rather than an arithmetic result; 11 and 12 are the tightness passes for add and sub.

author: reek
body: The innermost loops. Each iteration adds 1 to the check count and 2^32 to the packed accumulator on a containment failure; nothing is allocated. ivx-scan-id checks the value itself for membership, for the union and intersection passes.

author: reek
body: Two checks per pair: each endpoint of the kernel answer must equal the concrete result at its extremal corner.

author: reek
body: One handler per interval pair, chosen by operator code. Codes 1..7 build the kernel answer once and scan every member pair for containment. Code 8 checks that the union contains every member of both inputs. Code 9 checks that the intersection contains every value lying in both inputs; disjoint inputs give an empty scan range, which contributes nothing - exactly the contract. Codes 11 and 12 check add and sub tightness at the extremal corners.

author: reek
body: The one unary operator gets its own two-level enumeration over the 136 intervals. Mode 1 scans every member for containment of its negation; mode 2 checks tightness, the endpoints witnessed by negating the opposite corners.

author: reek
body: One line per operator with the exact check and failure counts, then the total. The expected file pins every number: a change in any count is a change in what was tested, and a nonzero failure count is an unsound transfer function.
